title: Fireworks AI Ads Strategy: The Inference Winner Advertises Training
summary: Fireworks AI is Ramp's top inference vendor, yet 155 of its 231 LinkedIn ads sell training and Forge. 115 Google ads chase every open-model launch.
body_markdown:
Ramp's October 2026 AI category data has Fireworks AI as the most-purchased Model Serving and Inference vendor. 27% of buyers in the category. It is also the most fragmented category on the list, so 27% is a lead, not a lock.


Then I opened the ads. Of 231 live LinkedIn ads, 23 sell inference or free credits. 155 sell something else: training your own model, a conference called Forge, and customers who trained one.


The inference winner advertises training. Search is where the inference ads went.


## Fireworks AI ads: key findings


- **0** Meta ads. Paid is 231 live LinkedIn ads and 115 Google ads
- **19** Google ads put the model's name in the display URL: /deepseekv4/get-started, /glm-5p3-flash/serverless, /kimi-k3/get-started
- **48 of 115** Google ads (42%) ride a model launch, from DeepSeek to GLM to Kimi
- **CompanyPostsBoosted** , **ABM1:1** and an unrenamed auto-generated boost: the campaign names behind Fireworks' tagged LinkedIn links
- **10** LinkedIn ads announce a model as live on day 0
- **9** Google ads open "Fireworks vs." Baseten, Cerebras, Groq or Together AI, paired with free credits
- **$100** in free credits is the LinkedIn offer. A self-serve account starts with $1
- **0** affiliate programs. Every incentive is credits
- **155 of 231** LinkedIn ads (67%) are about training, owning a model, Forge or customers who trained one


## How Fireworks' funnel is wired


Fireworks doesn't create demand for inference. Other labs do, every time they ship a model. The account is built to be standing there when they do.


### Every model release becomes an ad group


19 Google ads carry a model name in the display URL, across 10 paths: fireworks.ai/deepseekv4/get-started, /deepseek-v4p1/serverless, /glm-5p3-flash/serverless, /kimi-k3/get-started, /ember-1/serverless and more.


These are display paths, the two short fields Google lets you print after the domain. They aren't pages, and typed into a browser they 404. Fireworks writes the model into them so someone searching "DeepSeek V4 API" sees the model's name in the headline and again in the URL.


The template shows its seams. An ad announcing "Kimi K2.7 is Live on Fireworks" still carries the /deepseekv4/get-started path from the ad group it was cloned from. Another reads "Ox Alpha is GLM 5.3 Flash", naming the model behind a stealth release in the headline.


### LinkedIn is the boost button for day-0 posts


Fireworks' LinkedIn links carry their campaign names, and three of them describe the playbook.


Campaign name What it carried


CompanyPostsBoosted Day-0 launches: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 ("our 4th new model release this week") and Qwen3.8-Max


ABM1:1 The Kimi K3 launch video, sent to a list of named accounts


BoostPostWebsiteVisitsNovember11,2025at12:11AM The Kimi K2 Thinking launch post. That's LinkedIn's default name for a post boosted straight from the page, never renamed


The order is organic launch first, paid amplification after. 10 LinkedIn ads announce a model as live. The account-based campaign gets the same news as everyone else, aimed at the companies Fireworks most wants to hear it.


### Ramp's leaderboard, run as an ad


One single-image LinkedIn ad opens "Four of the top 10 trending vendors are AI inference platforms. Why?" and links to Ramp's May 2026 leading-indicators report. A paid ad sending its clicks to someone else's site, because the someone else is a spend index that ranks Fireworks. Attention's CEO and VP Growth run the same play.


## Credits, not commissions


There's no Fireworks affiliate program. /affiliates is a 404 and no partner rate is published. Every incentive is compute.


Offer Where it shows Terms


Free credits Google conquest ads ("Fireworks vs. Baseten", Groq, Together AI) "Get Started today with Free Credits"


$100 in free credits LinkedIn single-image ads "Start Building with $100 of Free Credits"


$1 credit Self-serve sign-up Every new account. When it runs out without a card on file, the account is suspended


Startup credits Not advertised Venture-backed with more than $500K raised, founded in the last five years, not past Series C. Credits expire after a year. No dollar amount published


AMD developer credits Not advertised $50, valid 90 days, through AMD's AI developer program


The gap between $1 and $100 is the funnel. A searcher who finds Fireworks on their own gets a dollar. One who arrives from a rival's name or a LinkedIn ad gets a hundred.


## LinkedIn is where Fireworks sells the next product


Almost none of the 231 LinkedIn ads explain what inference is. The buyer already has a model. The ads tell them they should not be renting it.


### Eight messages, mutually exclusive


Message cluster Ads Share Headline examples


Train and own your model 70 30% "Training API + Fireworks Lab are now generally available." (18), "Build intelligence that's uniquely yours." (18), "Make the Model Your Edge" (6)


Customer case studies 46 20% "Build your own legal frontier." (5), Cursor's Composer 2, Genspark, Heidi Health


Events 39 17% "Forge: Build Your Own Frontier" (24), "Forge | November 3 | San Francisco" (8), First Pour in Paris


Cost control 36 16% "Spend and ship, or ration tokens and stall?" (4), "More control over AI coding spend" (4), "Same workflow. 54% less AI spend." (2)


Model launches and benchmarks 15 6% "Kimi K3 is Live: see how it compares to Opus 5" (3), Muse Glimmer, Qwen, DeepSeek


Founder and thought-leader posts 9 4% Lin Qiao, the CEO, on rented versus owned intelligence


Free credits and generic inference 8 3% "Start Building with $100 of Free Credits" (2)


Jobs, follow, message and document formats 8 3% Four job ads, two message ads


The most-purchased inference vendor spends 3% of its LinkedIn ads on "start building with free credits." The old acquisition message is the smallest bucket on the page.


"Training API now generally available." The ad is a dashboard screenshot of a completed Kimi K3 fine-tuning run. Running 18 times.


### The copy: you write the loop, we run the rest


The Training API ad says "Frontier-level training shouldn't require frontier-lab infrastructure. You write the training loop and reward. Fireworks handles the trainer, rollouts, and infrastructure underneath it."


That is the same company that sells inference. The new product is a reason to stay, not a reason to leave. Train on Fireworks, serve on Fireworks.


### Harvey, Cursor, Genspark, Heidi


46 case-study ads, and they are not about speed. They are about a customer who built a model.


Customer Ads mentioning them The claim


Cursor 15 Composer 2, trained with large-scale RL, "6-10x lower inference cost"


Harvey 13 "Nearly twice the tasks completed at effectively flat cost"


Heidi Health 13 Latency cut 3.5x, from 25 seconds to 7, proof of concept to production in 4 weeks


Genspark 10 Gen-1 Slides, "About 90% less per deck than Opus 5"


Counts overlap because one ad can name Cursor and a conference. The pattern does not. Every named customer is a company whose own model is the product.


"Specialized intelligence for legal teams." Harvey is the proof point, and the button says "See how Harvey did it."


### The cost ads are a second product


36 ads cover cost control, and 27 name Nexus, a product that routes coding-tool traffic from tools like Claude Code and Codex to open models. "Spend and ship, or ration tokens and stall?" is the question. "Frontier intelligence. Half the bill." is the answer.


Nexus: 33% savings per merged PR, 54% overall AI spend saved, 100+ tokens a second.


The buyer here is a head of engineering with a token budget, not a developer with a prompt. A separate Fireworks ad quotes Ramp Economics Lab: four of the top 10 trending vendors are AI inference platforms, because teams are getting deliberate about which model handles which workload.


### The CEO is an ad unit


Nine posts run as founder or thought-leader content. Four run under Lin Qiao's own name, two of them Article ads, and two video ads carry her line that the future "will not be a small number of AGI models dominating the world... it will be millions of specialized" ones.


One Article ad argues that a company that owns its intelligence gets better every week and one that rents it is a policy change from starting over. That is the whole LinkedIn campaign in two sentences.


## Google is where the inference ads went


The 115 Google ads are almost all text. 112 text, 3 video. First shown 28 January 2025, and 68 were still showing in October 2026.


Headline cluster Ads Share What it says


Model launches and model pages 48 42% "DeepSeek V4 has Landed," "GLM 5.3 is open-weight and live on Fireworks," "Kimi K2.6 is on Fireworks AI," "Ember-1: Only on Fireworks"


Own and train your model 20 17% "Own your own AI with Fireworks," "Beat the Frontier on Your Domain," "Learn About Training with Fireworks"


Generic open-source inference 15 13% "Open-source AI Inference - Always Open. Always Fast"


Brand name only 13 11% "Fireworks AI" (10 near-identical)


Head-to-head comparisons 12 10% "Fireworks vs. Baseten," "vs. Groq," "vs. Together," "vs. Cerebras," "Compare Kimi K3 vs. Fable 5"


Case studies and cost proof 7 6% "How Juicebox Cut Latency by 80%," "Frontier Intelligence. Half the Bill."


### Open-model releases are search events


48 ads, one every time a lab ships. Kimi appears in 21 ads, DeepSeek in 13, GLM in 11, Qwen in 5. Many put the model in the display URL, like fireworks.ai/deepseekv4/get-started, so the model's name shows twice.


The timing is the tell. "Kimi K3 is Coming Soon" and waitlist ads ran 20 to 27 July. The Kimi K3 comparison ads first showed on 27 July. Fireworks was in the results before the model was live and stayed there after.


### The comparison layer


"Fireworks vs. Baseten" shows up in four separate ads. Groq, Together and Cerebras each get one or two. These people are comparing vendors and already typing a rival's name. Four more ads compare Kimi K3 to a closed model.


The strange part is how many of those pages say "Own." 20 headlines carry "Own your own AI" or training language, even on a query like "open-source AI inference." The LinkedIn story leaks into search.


## Why the split makes sense


LinkedIn Google


Ads 231 115


Train and own 70 (30%) 20 (17%)


Model launches 15 (6%) 48 (42%)


Comparison to rivals 0 12 (10%)


Events 39 (17%) 0


Cost control 36 (16%) 7 (6%)


Google buys intent. Someone types "DeepSeek V4 API" and Fireworks answers with a page for that model. LinkedIn buys a conversation with a team that has already picked a serving vendor, so the message is the next purchase.


Meta is not in the plan. No Meta ads at all.


## What actually makes this work


Fireworks does not market what it won. It markets what it wants to sell next.


The 27% of buyers already have the serving relationship. The training, the Nexus routing and the conference all build on it. Each ad gives that buyer a reason to put one more workload on the same vendor.


Search runs the reverse job. Every new open model is a fresh query, and Fireworks is the first ad on it. The two channels do not repeat each other, and neither one runs the "start building" message the category normally runs.


If your category's winner is a utility, look at what it sells on its second channel.
